ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, particularly the Société en Commandite Spéciale provisions introduced by Law of 23 July 2016; Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 11 March 2019 on the practical modalities of the Register of Beneficial Owners. Beneficial ownership is determined by direct or indirect ownership or control above 25% of capital or voting rights, or control by other means.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent authority of the jurisdiction of organisation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the country of origin; if the country is not a Hague Convention Contracting State, consular legalization at a Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports and proof of residential address for all natural-person UBOs, general partner if an individual, and authorised managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing national authority; proof of address issued by municipal registry, utility authority, financial institution or equivalent; signature certified by a notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where notarised; acceptable professional certified copies for EU/EEA documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the foreign jurisdiction or other authorised legalisation authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by Luxembourg notarial endorsement

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or company registry in the jurisdiction of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, general partner, managers, shareholders and UBOs against the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) indicators, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, and the OFAC SDN list. Politically exposed persons must be identified before engagement and subject to enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Adverse media and negative news screening is mandatory at onboarding and periodic review.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal and guichet.lu electronic filing platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name must use Latin-script characters and must be distinguishable from all names already recorded in the RCS. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters for the RCS filing and publication extract. The legal form may be expressed as SCSp or société en commandite spéciale; no civil-law company form suffix such as S.A. or S.à r.l. may be used. The name must not be misleading as to the legal form, activity, or connection with a public authority.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg / Luxembourgish where the name falsely implies official state sponsorship
Société Anonyme / S.A. where the entity is not an S.A.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects a name, the applicant may request a written reasoning from the Luxembourg Business Registers, promptly file a new reservation using a modified distinctive element, or seek reconsideration through an administrative petition to LBR. If refusal is maintained, a judicial action may be brought before the competent Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) in accordance with general administrative and commercial procedure. Name reservations may be renewed before expiry for additional preservation periods, provided the incorporation filing remains pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or mailbox-only address is not permissible. The SCSp must maintain a genuine Luxembourg registered office or administrative seat with physical presence, accessible books and records, and a local service capacity. A licensed serviced-office or domiciliation address with a physical Luxembourg office and dedicated letterbox is acceptable for this low-risk robotic AI toy hardware holding and trading activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk of approximately 20% in the first 36 months for a dormant or single-member SCSp; the likelihood increases if the SCSp files VAT, employs staff, claims tax treaty benefits, or uses a high-volume domiciliation provider. Unannounced inspections by the RCS, the Luxembourg tax administration, or the Financial Intelligence Unit in the context of AML/CFT audits are legally possible and cannot be excluded.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; SCSp regime under Articles 944-1 to 944-25; general provisions at Articles 1-7; Law of 23 July 2016 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitutive deed (acte de constitution) executed as a private deed or notarial deed, filed electronically with the RCS and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum share capital, paid-up capital, or escrow account requirement for an SCSp; the partners freely determine the amount of their contributions (apports) and the capital structure in the limited partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that each subscriber identified in Schedule I hereby subscribes for the partnership interests (parts d'intérêts) allocated to them and accepts the terms of the limited partnership agreement. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the SCSp be established at 12, Rue Guillaume Schneider, L-2522 Luxembourg, and that the general partner coordinate the adoption of that address for all official records and stationery. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the general partner appoints Mr. Marc Peters as Chief Operating Officer and day-to-day manager (dirigeant) with sole signature authority for administrative and banking matters, effective immediately, and ratifies the opening of bank accounts and the engagement of the registered agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and registered office preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS pre-filing desk via the LBR e-mail and e-filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name for a non-confusion certificate (certificat de non-confusion) and verify trademark availability. Secure a registered office address in Luxembourg City or commune of choice by executing a lease or domiciliation agreement. Retain the negative certificate for use at filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed name and trade name schedule
Identification of founders and general partner
Notarized or lawfully dated domiciliation agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS flags confusion or infringement risk, resubmit with written consent of the existing name holder or select alternative names; the negative certificate can be re-issued upon amendment through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary or, in default of real estate contributions, the partners acting by private deed (acte sous seing privé).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and settle the limited partnership agreement containing the identity of the general partner and limited partners, corporate purpose, registered office, duration, contribution schedule, profit-sharing, and governance powers. Each partner signs the deed and accepts their subscription; if a notary is engaged, the notary authenticates the deed and retains the original minute.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each partner
Proof of address of each partner
Declaration of acceptance by the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is requested due to real estate contribution, obtain a sworn real estate appraisal and a rectification deed; if private deed, correct the subscription schedule and have all partners re-sign before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, e-filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the signed constitutive deed, negative certificate, registered office proof, KYC/identity documents of the general partner and directors, and the appointment declaration. Make the registration and RESA publication fee payment online. The RCS assigns the registration number and effects the mandatory RESA publication upon approval.
required_dossiers: General partner acceptance and identity documents
Power of attorney if filed by a mandated agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any RCS query via the e-filing portal within 15 days; file a supplementary corrigendum or amended deed if required. Rejected applications may be refiled with a revised deed and an additional administrative fee; ensure cross-border verification of corporate names to avoid refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer, VAT, and social security registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), and Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the employer registration with the CCSS within eight days of commencing operations; register for VAT with the AEDT; declare the registered office and any employees through MyGuichet.lu. The SCSp must obtain its business identification number and, if employing staff, an ITM occupational declaration.
required_dossiers: Constitutive deed and limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS or AEDT raises an incompleteness notice, correct and resubmit the payroll and VAT forms within the indicated deadline; late or repeated omissions may subject the SCSp to administrative fines and delayed personnel declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Industry and SMEs, Division des autorisations, processed via MyGuichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the mandatory business establishment permit covering the manufacturing and commercial activity. Demonstrate that the natural person responsible for continuous management holds the required professional qualification and honorability. Upon approval, the Ministry issues the establishment card (carte d'établissement), which must be displayed at the registered office and renewed as required.
required_dossiers: Diploma, professional qualification certificate, or three years' relevant practice proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry declares the dossier incomplete, time limits are suspended until curing the identified defects. Submit the requested evidence within the notice period; adverse decisions can be challenged before the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within three months of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Division des autorisations, in coordination with the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development and the RCS.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) and establishment card (carte d'établissement), together with the classified installation environmental permit (commodo/incommodo) where applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement – Luxembourg Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B/Class 2 classified installation for assembly of electronic toys and lithium-polymer batteries; screening and simplified environmental impact notice (notice d'impact) rather than a full EIA report; WEEE (waste electrical and electronic equipment) registration required for battery and electronic components.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 January 2010 (maximum COD 125 mg/L, TSS 35 mg/L, pH 6-9, heavy metals below listed thresholds); volatile organic compounds must respect the solvent emission limits of Directive 2004/42/EC and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 27 June 2016; waste handling requires certified selective collection, packaging compliance, and traceability records; noise and air emissions from test benches and ventilation must remain below the quantitative thresholds of the 2018 regulated installations decree.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Administration des Services de Secours (fire and rescue service) covering alarm systems, evacuation routes, and extinguishing equipment; structural load inspection certificate from an accredited engineer for assembly and warehousing floors; occupational safety and health clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering machine guards, electrical installations, and battery handling protocols; construction permit (autorisation de bâtir) where fit-out alters load-bearing elements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating as a full Eurosystem member; prudential supervision of credit institutions and e-money institutions assigned to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); exchange-control and capital-movement policy administered jointly by the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance and BCL under the Law of 15 June 2004 on the free movement of capital and the EU Treaty Article 63 TFEU.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility: the euro is a freely convertible currency and Luxembourg maintains no IMF Article VIII restrictions, no exchange-control approvals, no quantitative ceilings, and no prior authorization for any current or capital account transaction. Capital account and current account flows are fully liberalized within the EU/EEA and towards third countries. For the SCSp, profit remittance and non-resident partner distributions face no legal restriction and no Luxembourg withholding tax at the entity level because the SCSp is fiscally transparent (pass-through) for Luxembourg income tax purposes. The only administrative burden is statistical balance-of-payments (BOP) reporting to the BCL for direct reporters, with a notification threshold of EUR 12,500 per individual transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no surrender requirement, no repatriation timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts obtained by resident legal entities or transparent partnerships. Foreign-currency export proceeds (USD, GBP, CNY) may be held indefinitely in multicurrency accounts at Luxembourg banks without forced conversion into EUR. The applicable obligation is purely statistical: BOP direct reporters must report each transaction equal to or exceeding EUR 12,500 to the BCL within the prescribed monthly/quarterly deadline; resident banks automatically cover the reporting for account-based flows unless the SCSp is registered as a direct BOP reporter.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multicurrency Account (EUR/USD/GBP) + Capital Contribution Collection Sub-account
Operational Account + Trade Finance Escrow Account (for LC/BD issuance)
Operational Account; Treasury Advisory Account with short-term EUR/USD deposit sweeps
Operational Account; Guarantee Escrow Account for standby letters of credit
Operational Account with SEPA Instant connectivity and API cash-management access

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (domestic payroll, utilities and leasing nexus)
Wealth and Partners' Distribution Account (advised, for non-resident partner income sweeps)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditional Medium. CSSF fully licensed Luxembourg e-money institutions (including Payconiq International and Decta Luxembourg) and prominent EU/UK EMI aggregators (Airwallex, Currencycloud, Revolut Business, Spendesk) can onboard an SCSp, but only where the general partner's legal identity, the partnership agreement, and the UBO list are fully disclosed and where the EMI supports partnership legal forms. Stripe, Adyen and other mass-market card acquirers commonly list the Luxembourg SCSp as an unsupported legal form for direct card acquiring; Stripe's published eligibility is primarily limited to SA, SARL, SCOP and sole trader; an SCSp therefore requires manual underwriting or a payment-facilitator arrangement via a Luxembourg payment institution. The pragmatic low-friction route is to maintain the operational account at BIL or BGL BNP Paribas, obtain a separate payment-facilitator contract from a Luxembourg-licensed EMI (Mangopay or Payconiq), and route Stripe/Credit-Card settlement into the SCSp collection account. For e-commerce retail of AI pet robots, this structure delivers full card acceptance without undermining the pass-through tax profile.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid mandate. Luxembourg CSSF Circular 19/716 (as amended) permits fully remote onboarding via video identification and qualified electronic signature for low-risk entities, and the AI pet-robot assembly business qualifies as standard low-risk under the CSSF AML/CFT framework. In practice, however, the major Luxembourg banks retain a discretionary one-time interview: at least one natural-person general partner (gérant) or an EU-resident authorized signatory must appear via a live video call, or physically if the bank requires it for foreign-controlled SCSp structures. Non-EU ultimate beneficial owners may not be required to travel, provided their identity and address verification documents are notarized, apostilled, and translated into English/French/German. A LuxTrust certificate or EU e-IDAS qualified electronic signature is required for all Luxembourg-resident signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent partnership classification disputed; bank flags the SCSp as a potential passive 'investment entity' under CRS/FATCA and demands full look-through of all limited partners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg tax transparency confirmation (Art. 185 LIR form or tax clearance letter), completed CRS Self-Certification Form A for all partners, extract from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), fully executed partnership agreement with English translation demonstrating active trading/manufacturing purpose, and the most recent interim or audited financial statements, if prepared.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layer-cake ownership triggers the 25% UBO disclosure test and the bank cannot identify the controlling natural persons because of discretionary trust or holding-company layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE registration certificate dated no older than three months, notarized corporate ownership chart with percentage annotations, individual client identification forms for every ultimate natural person above 25% of capital, source-of-wealth statement signed by the partners, and comfort letter from the Luxembourg registered agent (ELF) confirming compliance with the Law of 13 January 2019 on the RBE registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance suspicion: hardware assembly business with no Luxembourg factory, no local staff and no physical inventory is treated by banking compliance as a shell or letterbox vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid lease contract for Luxembourg registered office and logistics warehouse, payroll slips and employment contracts for at least two to five Luxembourg-based operations and compliance staff, supply-chain invoices from component suppliers, minutes of partner/management meetings held physically in Luxembourg, and a monthly sales ledger evidencing genuine commercial activity in the interactive robot market.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Enhanced due diligence triggered by cross-border trade flows: Chinese component sourcing and US/EU retail distribution raise concerns over export controls, counterfeit goods, and sanctions exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Self-classification letter confirming the AI pet robot is not ITAR/EAR-controlled and falls outside dual-use export restrictions, ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 27001 certificates, supplier due-diligence file for Chinese vendors (business licence translation, bank reference, no-evidence-of-sanctions undertaking), end-user undertaking for retail robotic goods, and a written compliance policy on product safety directives (EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection sourced from crypto exchange proceeds or non-EU private wealth is treated as unexplained or high-risk source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified withdrawal and fiat-conversion statements from regulated exchange platforms (FCA, CSSF, BaFin or equivalent licensed), bank reference letters from the sending institution, a source-of-wealth report prepared by a Luxembourg law firm or Big-4 adviser, and prior-year tax returns or corporate accounts of the contributing partners.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Parent or investor funds arrive via SWIFT MT103 with field 23E set to CRED and field 70 containing explicit purpose code in EPC/BoP format: S010 (equity participation) or NUC (non-financial incorporation) for an SCSp capital contribution. Beneficiary bank must be BIL (SWIFT BILLLULLX) or BGL BNP Paribas (SWIFT BNPALULL); beneficiary account field 59 must show the full legal name 'Name SCSp (Société en commandite spéciale)' and the dedicated capital contribution collection sub-account number. The bank requires a signed capital commitment schedule, the executed partnership agreement (or amendment), and the CSSF AML/KYC file to be forwarded at least two banking days before the wire. For SEPA-based intra-EU contributions, use a SEPA Credit Transfer with purpose code DGAR for guarantees or TRAD for trade-related advances. Any single transaction equal to or over EUR 12,500 must be flagged to the BCL BOP reporting team; the account bank will generate the obligatory BOP declaration automatically if the SCSp is not a direct reporter.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements leverage a tiered clearing architecture: (i) SEPA Instant or SEPA Credit Transfer for EU component suppliers; (ii) SWIFT MT103 with field 70 referencing the commercial invoice number for USD and GBP suppliers through the BGL/BIL international clearing network; (iii) Irrevocable Confirmed Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) issued by BGL or BIL under UCP600 for large Chinese or US vendor batches, with INCOTERMS 2020 such as CIF or FOB; (iv) Standby Letters of Credit (SBLC) as advance-payment protection for tooling and mould purchases; and (v) direct custodial CNY clearing via BGL's CNH correspondent network for settlements with Shenzhen and Guangzhou manufacturers. All outbound payments above EUR 12,500 are captured by the bank's BCL BOP reporting duty; the SCSp must instruct each payment with a precise trade/import purpose code to avoid classification as a financial transaction and subsequent CMS (Customs and Measures) review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable vanilla forwards (tenor 1-12 months) executed OTC with BGL BNP Paribas or BIL under the 2002 ISDA Master Agreement; exempt from EMIR clearing when the hedge notional remains below the EUR 3,000,000 clearing threshold.

EUR/CNY deliverable FX forwards (CNH leg) and onshore CNY swaps for component-import cost protection; for CNH tenors where physical delivery is impossible, a non-deliverable forward (NDF) referencing the CNH fixing is permissible as a statutory hedge for 90-180 day procurement exposure.
EUR/USD cross-currency swaps under ISDA/CSA with the Luxembourg treasury desk to convert committed USD retail revenue into EUR operating liquidity.
EUR/USD OTC FX options (call or put, capped premiums) for upside protection on large seasonal inventory purchases and trade receivables, supported by the underlying supply-purchase agreements.
Plain vanilla EUR/USD currency swaps executed with the relationship bank for match-funding of the US retail receivables facility, documented under the standard EMIR-compliant CSA schedule.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts preparation and RCS publication (when the SCSp is within the filing obligation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year SCSp: within one month after approval by the partners and in any event no later than seven months after financial-year end (31 July). A private SCSp without legal personality is normally exempt from publication unless a general partner is a corporate entity or group thresholds make filing compulsory.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the filing obligation exists, late or non-filing triggers coercive daily fines up to EUR 250, criminal fines ranging from EUR 500 to 5,000, and a possible judicial strike-off of the RCS registration after repeated defaults.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual reconfirmation of beneficial-owner data (UBO annual declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), administered by LBR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following the annual anniversary of the SCSp's RBE registration; no uniform calendar date applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Risk of administrative fine up to EUR 10,000 per violation; deliberate false or omitted data may trigger criminal sanctions under the amended Law of 13 January 2019.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% CIT; plus 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT (18.19% combined); municipal business tax (Luxembourg City 6.75%) yields approximately 24.94% aggregate for taxable corporates; SCSp is fiscally transparent by default (no entity-level CIT) unless it elects corporate taxation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays. Preferential measures: IP Box regime (80% exemption on net qualifying IP income; effective CIT rate approximately 5.25%), investment tax credit for qualifying tangible assets, R&D tax credit, unlimited loss carry-forward, and participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory time limit since 2017; Article 114 LIR)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate/partnership income tax declaration filed electronically via the ACD eCDF portal (accessible through MyGuichet.lu). Taxable corporate SCSp: Form 760 (Corporate Income Tax, Municipal Business Tax and Net Wealth Tax). Transparent SCSp: annual partnership income declaration with partner allocation schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December of the year following the fiscal year (e.g., fiscal year ending 31 December 2025 is due 31 December 2026); earlier deadlines may be published; extension requests are filed electronically.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer name, RCS number, registered office, fiscal year and competent tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must be listed with foreign tax identification and residence address; the Luxembourg fiscal agent signs on behalf of the partnership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss before tax allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full result from the Luxembourg permanent establishment; do not net foreign-source income outside the PE against Luxembourg losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses, fines, 50% of certain payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, and excessive financing costs under the ATAD interest limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest and royalties paid by the SCSp to a related non-resident in a non-cooperative state must be added back and trigger the 20% anti-abuse withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption, IP Box deduction (80%), depreciation, and treaty-based deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach supporting schedules and tax residency certificates where treaty or EU directive relief is claimed at partner level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year losses offset against current taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a transparent SCSp, loss allocation follows the partnership agreement percentages and must be supported by audited accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed Luxembourg taxable basis and allocation among partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the partner allocation schedule; non-resident partners report the allocated share in their residence state and claim foreign tax credit or treaty relief where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted filing triggers taxation d'office (estimated assessment), an administrative fine up to EUR 1,500, and monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% on the tax due. Fraudulent filings attract criminal tax fraud sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax for Luxembourg taxable corporations; 0% withholding tax on distributions by a transparent SCSp because the distribution is a profit share, not a dividend. If the SCSp elects corporate taxation, the 15% WHT applies, with 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (10% participation, 12-month holding) and a 50% exemption in certain domestic cases.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident partner must: (1) hold a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its state of residence; (2) file the ACD exemption or refund application through the Luxembourg withholding agent or directly with the ACD via eCDF/MyGuichet; (3) demonstrate beneficial ownership and absence of an artificial conduit arrangement. Claims generally must be made within five years of the distribution date.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg statutory WHT on outbound royalties and interest is 0%. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive grants 0% for associated EU companies. DTA treaty rates typically range from 0% to 10%. Anti-abuse rule: a 20% WHT and non-deductibility apply to interest and royalties paid to related recipients in non-cooperative jurisdictions, effective since 2021.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: required where aggregate related-party transactions of the Luxembourg entity exceed EUR 1,000,000 (administrative guidance). Master File: required where the MNE group consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 100,000,000. Country-by-Country Report: mandatory where consolidated group revenue is at least EUR 750,000,000 (Law of 23 December 2016).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no offshore-style ESR statute. Substance is nonetheless a decisive anti-abuse requirement: the SCSp must maintain local administration, registered offices, decision-making, adequate staff and assets to avoid characterization as an artificial arrangement under the EU ATAD GAAR (implemented by the Law of 21 December 2018) and to retain treaty access and the participation exemption. A corporate general partner is required to be established in Luxembourg or the EEA for a valid SCSp.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful failure to file the annual SCSp income declaration, deliberate understatement of AI pet robot sales revenue, or fabrication of inflated costs to eliminate Luxembourg taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of evaded tax plus a 10% administrative increase and 0.6% monthly late-payment interest; criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 or double the evaded tax; imprisonment from 1 month to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner (commandité) is jointly and severally liable for SCSp debts; managing directors can be ordered to pay civil restitution from personal assets, face freezing orders and travel bans, and serve imprisonment in serious fraud cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SCSp solely as a conduit to hold IP and receive royalties from the AI pet robot without personnel, premises or economic rationale, or structuring round-trip financing to drain profits to a non-cooperative jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the structure; denial of treaty benefits and the participation exemption; taxation of reclassified flows at the aggregate Luxembourg CIT/municipal rate (approximately 24.94%) plus a 10% penalty and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved the artificial scheme are personally liable for the resulting tax shortfall if the SCSp is insolvent; disqualification from board positions and travel bans may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting related-party prices for robot components, IP royalties or management fees outside the arm's length range without a benchmarking study, or failing to document the arm's length methodology.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer pricing adjustment increasing taxable income; denial of deduction for undocumented payments; compensatory adjustment; 10% late-filing surcharge; 0.6% monthly late-payment interest on the incremental tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors who sign inaccurate transfer pricing documentation face civil liability for the additional tax and penalties in the event of bankruptcy; criminal liability attaches when mispricing is used as a tax fraud instrument.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file or update the SCSp's ultimate beneficial owners in the Luxembourg Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), or failure to maintain proper accounting and AML records (KYC, source-of-funds evidence).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines between EUR 125 and EUR 250,000 (or up to EUR 1,250,000 for serious or repeated violations); blocking of profit distributions; criminal sanctions for intentional false declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The manager and directors may be personally fined for each month of non-compliance, face criminal proceedings for money-laundering facilitation, and be subject to travel bans and confiscation of assets derived from the non-compliant structure.
